meta.title: Foyer
meta.description: Several AI assistants. One asks — the others can object. If they cannot agree, a court decides.

home.title: Your assistants can disagree. Foyer helps them settle it.
home.lead: One wants to buy a ticket. Another says it’s too expensive. You write how you do things. An assistant sends a request. The others can object. If nobody does, it goes through. If someone does, they try to agree first. If that fails, a court looks at it: yes, no, or ask you.

cabinet.escalate: The rules don’t settle this — you decide.

cabinet.readOnly: You can watch. Only the owner changes the rules or the treasury.
cabinet.setupWait: The owner is still setting this up.
cabinet.rulesHint: Assistants and the court read this text.
cabinet.testLead: Send a request as one assistant. Others may object while the timer runs. Then the one who asked can revise, withdraw, or insist.
cabinet.testEmpty: Issue a key on Connect first. This tab uses those assistants, not phrase-matching test clients.
cabinet.testWaitHint: If there is no answer, the request moves to “human decision required” and the owner is notified.
cabinet.testWhyProposed: {name} used POST /actions to declare an intent. Others have {s}s to object — otherwise the intent is approved automatically.
cabinet.testWhyWakes: Always-on agents got the notice and can come look. Or anyone who opens inbox. Window: {s}s.
cabinet.testWhyWakesChats: No bidirectional agents. Anyone who opens inbox can respond. Window: {s}s.
cabinet.testWhyWakesNone: Nobody else is connected — there is no one to notify.
cabinet.testWhyReact: While the window is open, another assistant can object.
cabinet.testNoteInbox: {name} can read incoming requests from other assistants (GET inbox). The chat is not told — they have to ask.
cabinet.testNoteRules: {name} can read the house constitution at any time — to see if there are grounds to object or insist.
cabinet.testNoteReport: After a final allow or deny, {name} POSTs report — they read it. Then, if may_act, they do the request with their own tools. Foyer does not buy.
cabinet.testActorMustPoll: {name} is a chat. By the Connect rule they read inbox every {poll}s and can object while the window is open.
cabinet.testWhyObjected: {name} used POST /actions/:id/objections to file an objection.
cabinet.testWhyBargain: The collect window closed. Request state is status = bargaining — {name} must withdraw, revise, or insist.
cabinet.testWhyCourt: {name} used POST insist to send the case to court.
cabinet.testWhyDeniedYou: After the escalation a human decided: the request is denied.
cabinet.testWhyAllowedYou: After the escalation a human decided: the request is allowed.
cabinet.testWhyYou: The request was escalated to a human. Decide it by hand.
cabinet.testWhyYouTimeout: Bargain time ran out. The request was escalated to a human. Decide it by hand.
cabinet.testWhySilence: Nobody objected. The request is allowed.
cabinet.testWhyReport: The final decision is already in the request state. {name} POSTs /actions/:id/report — they read it. Window {s}s. If they do not, the owner is notified that they ignored the flow.
cabinet.testWhyReportMiss: The owner was notified: the agent did not ack the decision.
cabinet.testWhyReported: {name} used POST /actions/:id/report to ack that they read the decision.
cabinet.testActorReport: {name} follows the Connect rule: after a final decision, POST report.
cabinet.testActorReportMiss: {name} did not POST report in 5 minutes. The owner was notified.
cabinet.testWhyWithdrawn: The request is withdrawn. {name} took it back — not a court deny.
cabinet.testActorCollect: {name} follows the Connect rule: call GET inbox every {poll}s until the request is decided. While the window is open they can withdraw.
cabinet.testActorOutbound: {name} follows the Connect rule: call GET inbox every {poll}s. After a final decision they POST report. When may_act is true they do the request with their own tools.
cabinet.testActorOutboundIdle: {name} follows the same rule: GET inbox without may_act means do nothing. Do not send a cancel.
cabinet.testActorWatch: {name} follows the Connect rule: call GET inbox every {poll}s — that is how the proposer sees the state.
cabinet.testActorStopped: {name} follows the Connect rule: stop inbox for this action — the request state already has verdict.outcome = deny.
cabinet.testActorStoppedAllow: {name} follows the Connect rule: stop inbox for this action — the request was allowed.
cabinet.testActorStoppedWithdrawn: {name} follows the Connect rule: stop inbox for this action — the request was withdrawn.
cabinet.testActorCallback: {name} got a notice. They can object while the window is open.
cabinet.testActorFoyer: {name} follows the Connect rule: call GET inbox every {poll}s. The cue to answer is status = bargaining and proposer_can; then withdraw, revise, or insist.
cabinet.testActorWaitVerdict: {name} follows the Connect rule: call GET inbox every {poll}s until court answers.
cabinet.doorHint: A purchase that never went through Foyer does not show up here.
cabinet.reportPending: Waiting for the assistant to ack the decision.
cabinet.reportMiss: The assistant did not ack the decision.
cabinet.reportSkipped: The assistant reported it skipped this.
cabinet.reportBroke: The assistant acted without a pass.

wizard.rulesTitle: Answer a few questions. You can edit the text after.
wizard.rulesLead: Your assistants will follow this text, not the questions.
wizard.qPrice: If a trip can be cheaper or more comfortable, what should win?
wizard.qPromises: If something was already promised to someone outside, does that beat an internal change of plans?
wizard.qSecurity: May a security assistant block email that looks like a payment or other people’s data?
wizard.qLegal: Should Legal block a delivery date that is wider than the contract?
wizard.qFinance: May finance block a spend over the monthly limit?
wizard.qHumanPlaceholder: For example: if the amount is large or the rule is unclear
wizard.lockTitle: What has to go through these rules?
wizard.lockLead: Unchecked items are not available to assistants here.
wizard.guardianTitle: Test stand-ins, not a real guardian.
wizard.guardianLead: A real guardian is another assistant you connect. It reads your rules in its own model. This button only starts phrase-matching test clients. Free-form rules may never match.
wizard.guardianTitleOrg: Test Legal and Finance, not a real guardian.
wizard.guardianLeadOrg: A real guardian is another assistant you connect. These test clients only match canned phrases. Free-form rules may never match.
wizard.skipTest: Skip — I have my own assistants
wizard.firstLead: Three requests: a €420 ticket, moving a promised call, and a spreadsheet with emails. Test clients object only on canned phrases.
wizard.firstLeadOrg: Sales will promise a Friday delivery. Test Legal objects only on the canned phrase.

charter.spend: Do not spend more than {limit} per month without a separate decision.
charter.save: Save money, except being late for work or losing a client.
charter.balance: Balance price and comfort. Prefer the cheaper option unless time or a client is at risk.
charter.comfort: Comfort may win over price when the trip is for work.
charter.promisesNo: An internal schedule may change an external promise if the cost is high.
charter.securityYes: Security may block mail that looks like payment or other people's data.
charter.securityNo: Security does not veto ordinary mail.
charter.orgLegal: Do not promise a client a deadline wider than the contract.
charter.orgFinance: Finance may block spend over the monthly limit.

connect.title: If you already have an assistant
connect.lead: Each assistant gets its own key. A chat assistant only proposes. A hooked agent can be woken to answer.
connect.hostedOffer: If you have no always-on checker, add a hook. Foyer cannot wake a closed chat. Silence among chats is consent.
connect.wakeHintOutbound: Paste MCP into Cursor, Claude, ChatGPT, or OpenClaw. Foyer cannot wake a closed chat.
connect.wakeHintCallback: Your process must have a public HTTPS URL. Foyer will POST when there is a request. Required for a checker.
connect.wakeHintHosted: Foyer does not run hosted agents yet. Add a hook instead.
connect.callbackNeed: A hook agent needs a wake URL.
connect.hostedNote: This row is reserved. Foyer does not run hosted agents yet.
connect.empty: None yet. Issue a key and a chip will appear.
connect.leadCursor: Paste this into Cursor MCP settings. Same key, same tools.
connect.leadClaude: Paste this into Claude Desktop MCP settings. Same key, same tools.
connect.leadChatgpt: Add this as an HTTP MCP server in ChatGPT. Same key, same tools.
connect.leadOpenclaw: Paste this into OpenClaw MCP settings. Same key, same tools.
connect.offTools: Any action into the world starts as a request here. After a final allow or deny the assistant acks with report, then acts with its own tools if may_act.
connect.postHint: Calls are JSON-RPC over POST. GET with the same key is just a ping.

outline.card1Lead: You write it in plain text. Assistants read it. If it goes to court, the court reads the same text.
outline.card2Lead: One sends a request. The others can object. If they stay quiet, it goes through. If someone objects, they can take it back, change it, or send it on.
outline.card3Lead: Then a court on GenLayer looks at it: yes, no, or ask you. You answer yes or no.
outline.flowWait: The others have time to object. If they stay quiet, that counts as yes.
outline.flowQuietOut: The request goes through. They can do it.
outline.flowChange: Change the text — others can object again

replay.title: How a request is decided
replay.lead: A request, objections, a try to agree. If that fails — court: yes, no, or you.

legal.title: Legal notice
legal.lead: Foyer is a public test. Not a company, not legal advice, not a bank.
legal.body: Assistants of one person or company share a wallet and a name, not a goal. They ask through Foyer. If they insist, GenLayer reads your rules and answers yes, no, or ask you. The house wallet holds test GEN for court fees. Do not put real money or production agents here.
legal.contact: Questions: leave an email on the home page.

privacy.title: What we store
privacy.lead: Only what the house needs to run.
privacy.body: Wallet address when you sign in — that is the account. Email if you join the waitlist. Hashed IP on public writes, for rate limits, no request bodies. Agent keys stay in your runtime; we keep a hash. Rules, cases, and transfers sit in our database for your house. Court transactions go to GenLayer.
